findings.title: Rejected device is cached as tagged, so later requests bypass the limit
findings.body: tagDeviceUI sets the device key in localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and never removes it when that call fails. When the limit is reached, CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and the first request is rejected, but the key stays cached for about 29 minutes. Every later request from that device ID hits the cache check at the top of tagDeviceUI, returns nil, and Authenticate succeeds. The device is never counted, so after one rejection it keeps anonymous access for the rest of the cache window. The fix is to cache the key only after a successful tag, or to delete it on error. No test covers a second request after a rejection.

findings.title: Requests without a device ID or a parseable IP skip the limit entirely
findings.body: TagDevice returns nil before any limit check when the X-Grafana-Device-Id header is empty (line 121), and also when the remote address cannot be parsed (line 128). Authenticate then proceeds and grants anonymous access. The device ID is fully client-supplied, so a client that omits the header is never counted or rejected, and the limit cannot be enforced for those requests once it is reached. Anonymous requests that are not tagged should be checked against the limit, or rejected when the limit is reached.

findings.title: Device tagging moved onto the synchronous login path using the request context
findings.body: Previously tagging ran in a goroutine with a detached 2-minute context and panic recovery. Now Authenticate waits for TagDevice on the request context. For every device not in the cache, login blocks on a DB write and, when a limit is configured, on a COUNT over the 30-day window (CreateOrUpdateDevice). If the client disconnects, the request context is cancelled and the write may fail with context canceled. The device key has already been cached at impl.go:87, so the device stays untagged for about 29 minutes. Only the limit check needs to be synchronous. The tagging write should not depend on the request context, or the cache entry should be cleared on failure.

findings.title: Device limit check is not atomic with the insert
findings.body: CountDevices and the following INSERT are separate statements with no transaction or lock. Concurrent first-time requests from distinct devices can each see count < deviceLimit and all insert, so the number of devices can exceed the configured limit by up to the number of concurrent first requests. The limit is therefore soft. If it is meant to be strict (for example for licensing), the check and insert need to be a single conditional statement or a transaction.

findings.title: Constructor signature changed for a DI-wired provider without any wire changes
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes db.DB instead of anonstore.AnonStore, and ProvideAnonDBStore now requires a deviceLimit argument. These are Wire providers, but no wire.go or wire_gen.go file is in the change set. If the generated injector still passes an AnonStore into this constructor, the build breaks. In either case the service now constructs its own store, so the AnonStore can no longer be injected or replaced in tests. The generated wiring needs to be checked and regenerated.

findings.title: New device_limit option is not documented
findings.body: The [auth.anonymous] device_limit key is parsed here, but it is not added to conf/defaults.ini or the configuration docs, and the PR's docs checkbox is unchecked. Operators cannot discover the option or its semantics: 0 means unlimited, the count covers devices updated in the last 30 days, and negative values are treated as unlimited.

findings.title: Device limit tests miss the update path and the request-level behavior
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the store level with limit 1. It does not cover an already-known device still being updated once the limit is reached (the updateDevice path). It also does not test TagDevice or Authenticate, where the rejected-device caching bug at impl.go:87 lives, so a retry after rejection is never checked. There is no test for a limit above 1 either.

findings.title: updateDevice comment and error description do not match behavior
findings.body: The comment says the function updates a device 'that has been updated between the given times', but it takes no time arguments. The window is hard-coded relative to device.UpdatedAt (30 days back to 1 minute ahead). The function also returns ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever no row matches, which includes devices that simply expired or were deleted concurrently. The comment and the error meaning should be corrected.
